Whole Masoor Dal Gravy recipe
A simple, healthy whole brown lentil curry with a light onion-tomato gravy — high in protein and fiber, easy weeknight comfort food.
Ingredients: (2 servings)
120 milliliters whole masoor (brown lentils), rinsed
360 milliliters water (for pressure cooking lentils)
1 tablespoons oil or ghee
0.5 medium onion, finely chopped
1 medium tomatoes, finely chopped
0.5 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
0.5 green chili, slit
0.5 teaspoons cumin seeds
0.3 teaspoons turmeric powder
0.5 teaspoons red chili powder
0.5 teaspoons coriander powder
0.3 teaspoons garam masala
0.5 teaspoons salt, to taste
1 tablespoons fresh coriander leaves, chopped
60 milliliters water (to adjust gravy consistency)
Steps
1.Cook the lentils: Pressure cook 120 milliliters whole masoor (brown lentils), rinsed with 360 milliliters water (for pressure cooking lentils) and a pinch of 0.3 teaspoons turmeric powder for 4-5 whistles, or until soft but still holding shape. (Stovetop: simmer covered 15 minutes.)
2. Temper the spices: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee in a pan. Add 0.5 teaspoons cumin seeds and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
3.Sauté onions: Add 0.5 medium onion, finely chopped and cook until golden brown, about 6 minutes
4.Add ginger-garlic and chili: Stir in 0.5 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste and 0.5 green chili, slit, cook for a minute until the raw smell goes away.
5.Cook the tomatoes: Add 1 medium tomato, finely chopped along with 0.5 teaspoons red chili powder, 0.5 teaspoons coriander powder and 0.5 teaspoons salt, to taste. Cook until the tomatoes turn soft and the oil separates, about 8 minutes.
6.Combine with lentils: Add the cooked 120 milliliters whole masoor (brown lentils), rinsed (with their cooking liquid) into the masala. Pour in 60 milliliters water (to adjust gravy consistency) to adjust consistency and mix well.
7.Simmer: Let the gravy simmer gently for 10 minutes so the flavors blend, stirring occasionally.
8.Finish and serve: Sprinkle in 0.3 teaspoons garam masala and 1 tablespoon fresh coriander leaves, chopped. Give it a final stir and serve hot with rice or roti.

HEALTHY SPINACH CHICKEN SHAWARMA WRAP RECIPE:
Ingredients (Makes 2 wraps)
For the chicken shawarma
300 g boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced
1 tbsp plain Greek yogurt
1 tsp olive oil
1 tsp paprika
1 tsp cumin
½ tsp coriander powder
½ tsp turmeric
½ tsp garlic powder (or 2 cloves minced garlic)
¼ tsp black pepper
½ tsp salt
Juice of ½ lemon
For the wrap
2 spinach wraps or whole-wheat wraps
1 cup shredded lettuce
1 small cucumber, sliced
1 tomato, diced
¼ red onion, thinly sliced
Healthy yogurt sauce
½ cup plain Greek yogurt
1 tbsp lemon juice
½ tsp black and white pepper Pinch of salt
Chopped parsley or mint (optional)
Instructions
Marinate the chicken
Mix yogurt, olive oil, spices, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 30 minutes (overnight is even better).
Cook the chicken
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken for 4–6 minutes per side until browned and fully cooked.
Let rest for a few minutes, then slice.
Make the sauce
Combine all yogurt sauce ingredients and stir until smooth.
Assemble the wraps
Warm the wraps briefly.
Spread yogurt sauce down the center.
Add lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onion, and chicken.
Roll tightly and slice in half.
Approximate Nutrition (per wrap)
Calories: 350–450
Protein: 30–35 g
Carbohydrates: 25–35 g
Fat: 10–15 g
Fiber: 5–8 g
To Make It Even Healthier
Use extra vegetables such as cabbage, bell peppers, or spinach.
Replace some sauce with hummus.
Use low-fat Greek yogurt.
Serve with a side salad instead of fries.

Fat-Loss Mango Blueberry Chia Pudding
Lower sugar, high fiber, filling, and good for calorie control.
Ingredients (1 serving)
2 tbsp chia seeds
1 tbsp rolled oats
3/4 cup unsweetened almond milk
1/4 cup mango (small amount for flavor)
1/4 cup blueberries
2 tbsp plain low-fat Greek yogurt
Pinch of cinnamon or cardamom
Instructions
Mix chia seeds and almond milk in a jar or bowl and roasted rolled oats.
Stir well, wait 5 minutes, then stir again.
Refrigerate overnight or at least 4 hours.
Add Greek yogurt and mix lightly.
Top with mango and blueberries.

🥭 Healthy Mango Pancakes (Weight-Loss Friendly)
Ingredients:
½ cup oats (blend into flour)
¼ cup ripe mango puree
1 egg (or 2 egg whites for lower calories)
2–3 tbsp yogurt
Pinch of baking powder
Cinnamon or cardamom (optional)
Method:
Blend everything into a smooth batter
Cook on a non-stick pan with minimal oil
Make small pancakes for better portion control
👍 Why this works for weight loss
Oats → slow-digesting carbs, keeps you full
Eggs/yogurt → protein reduces cravings
Mango → natural sweetness, no added sugar
⚠️ What to avoid
No maple syrup or honey (adds unnecessary calories)
Avoid refined flour (maida)
Don’t overdo mango—keep it moderate
🥄 Smart toppings
A spoon of plain yogurt
Chia seeds or flaxseeds
A few chopped nuts
Portion tip
Stick to 2–3 small pancakes + protein topping. Even healthy pancakes can slow weight loss if you overeat.

Low-Fat Matcha Latte recipe:
Ingredients
1 tsp Matcha (about 2 g)
1/4 cup hot water (not boiling; ~80°C)
1 cup low-fat milk (1–2% fat)
Optional:
1 tsp honey or maple syrup
Stevia or another zero-calorie sweetener
Ice for iced version
Instructions
Sift the matcha into a cup to avoid clumps.
Add hot water and whisk in a zig-zag motion until frothy.
Heat the low-fat milk and froth if desired.
Pour milk into the matcha mixture.
Sweeten to taste.
Calories (Approx.)
Ingredient
Calories
Matcha (1 tsp)
5–10 kcal
Low-fat milk (1 cup / 240 ml)
100–125 kcal
Honey (1 tsp, optional)
~20 kcal
Stevia
0 kcal
Total
Unsweetened: ~110–130 kcal
With 1 tsp honey: ~130–150 kcal
Higher-Protein Option
Use high-protein low-fat milk or add a scoop of unflavored protein powder for a more filling drink.
Iced Café-Style Version
Blend:
1 tsp matcha
1 cup chilled low-fat milk
Ice
1–2 tsp vanilla syrup or sweetener
That usually stays under 150 kcal if lightly sweetened.

🍓 Strawberry Oatmeal Yogurt Jar (Fat-Loss | 1 Serving)
🧾 Ingredients
Rolled oats – 3 tbsp
Low-fat curd / Greek yogurt – ½ cup (120–150 g)
Strawberries (chopped) – 5–6 medium
Chia seeds – 1 tsp
Cinnamon powder – a pinch
Honey / dates – NOT needed (optional: stevia only)
Water or milk – 2–3 tbsp (to soften oats)
👩‍🍳 Method (Jar Style)
Soak oats with water/milk for 10–15 minutes (or overnight).
In a jar/glass, add:
First layer: soaked oat
Second layer: yogurt
Third layer: chopped strawberries
Sprinkle chia seeds + cinnamon on top.
Mix slightly or keep layered.
Refrigerate overnight or eat fresh.
🔢 Approx Nutrition
Calories: ~230–250 kcal
Protein: ~12–14 g
Fiber: ~6 g
Sugar: natural only (from fruit)

🌾 Ragi Uttapam Recipe (Healthy)
🧾 Ingredients (2 servings)
Ragi flour – 1 cup
Curd (low-fat) – ½ cup
Water – as needed (to make thick batter)
Onion (finely chopped) – 1 small
Tomato (finely chopped) – 1 small
Capsicum / Carrot (finely chopped) – 2 tbsp
Green chilli (optional) – 1, finely chopped
Ginger (grated) – ½ tsp
Cumin seeds – ½ tsp
Salt – to taste
Oil – 1–2 tsp (use minimal)
👩‍🍳 Method
In a bowl, mix ragi flour + curd + water to make a thick, lump-free batter.
Add salt and cumin seeds. Mix well.
Let the batter rest for 10–15 minutes (important for softness).
Heat a non-stick tawa and lightly grease it.
Pour a ladle of batter and gently spread (keep it thick like uttapam).
Sprinkle onion, tomato, veggies, ginger, and chilli on top.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.
Cook on medium flame till the base is crisp.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes.
Serve hot.
🥗 Serving Suggestions
Coconut chutney (less coconut, more roasted chana)
Mint chutney
Plain curd or vegetable sambar

🍓 Strawberry Whey Protein Oatmeal Shake (1 Serving)
🧾 Ingredients
Rolled oats – 2 tbsp
Strawberry (fresh or frozen) – 5–6 medium
Whey protein (unflavoured or vanilla) – 1 scoop
Low-fat milk or unsweetened almond milk – 200 ml
Chia seeds or flaxseed powder – 1 tsp
Cinnamon powder – a pinch
Ice cubes – optional
👩‍🍳 Method
Dry roast oats lightly (optional, improves digestion). Let cool.
Add oats, strawberries, whey protein, milk, seeds, cinnamon to a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Adjust thickness with water if needed.
Consume immediately.
🔢 Approx Nutrition (approx.)
Calories: ~280–300 kcal
Protein: ~25–28 g
Fiber: ~6–7 g
Fat: ~5 g

🥗 Diabetic-Friendly Tofu Wrap Recipe
Ingredients (1 Wrap)
For the tofu filling
Tofu (firm) – 50g, crumbled or cubed
Olive oil – ½ tsp
Onion – 2 tbsp, finely chopped
Capsicum (any color) – ¼ cup, chopped
Cabbage – ¼ cup, shredded
Garlic – 1–2 cloves, minced
Tomato (firm, low-acid) – ¼ cup, chopped
Turmeric – ¼ tsp
Black pepper – ¼ tsp
Red chilli flakes – optional, a pinch
Salt – to taste
Lemon juice – 1 tsp
Fresh coriander – 1 tbsp, chopped
For the wrap
Whole wheat roti / multigrain tortilla / ragi roti – 1 piece
Low-fat curd or hung curd dressing – 1 tbsp (mix curd + pinch of salt + roasted jeera + black pepper)
Instructions
1. Prepare tofu filling
Heat ½ tsp olive oil.
Add garlic & onions → sauté 1 min.
Add capsicum, cabbage, tomato → cook for 2–3 mins on medium flame.
Add tofu → mix well.
Add turmeric, pepper, chilli flakes & salt.
Cook 3–4 mins until slightly dry.
Switch off flame → add lemon juice & coriander.
2. Assemble the wrap
Warm the whole-wheat or multigrain wrap.
Spread 1 tbsp curd dressing.
Add the tofu filling.
Roll tightly and toast on a dry pan for 1 minute for crispiness.
Nutrition (Approx)
Calories: 260–290 kcal
Protein: 17–20g
Carbs: 26–30g (low GI)
Fat: 8–10g
Fiber: 5–7g

Healthy Paneer Sandwich recipe.
🕒 Prep Time: 10 mins
🍳 Cook Time: 5–7 mins
🍽️ Serves: 2 sandwiches
🧀 Ingredients:
Paneer (cottage cheese) – 1/2 cup (crumbled or grated)
2 Whole wheat multigrain roti  / multigrain / brown bread – 4 slices
Capsicum (bell pepper) – 1/4 cup (finely chopped)
Onion – 1 small (finely chopped)
Tomato – 1 small (deseeded & chopped)
Coriander leaves – 1 tbsp (chopped)
Green chili – 1 (optional, finely chopped)
Black pepper – 1/4 tsp
Chaat masala / cumin powder – 1/4 tsp (optional)
Salt – to taste
Low-fat curd / hung curd / green chutney – 1–2 tsp (optional, for spread)
Butter / ghee / olive oil – for toasting (optional, 1/2 tsp per sandwich)
🥣 Filling Preparation:
In a bowl, mix:
Crumbled paneer
Capsicum, onion, tomato
Green chili (if using), coriander leaves
Salt, pepper, chaat masala or cumin
Mix gently to combine. Keep it dry (avoid excess moisture).
🥪 To Assemble & Cook:
Spread curd or green chutney on one side of bread (optional).
Add filling on one slice. Cover with another slice.
Toast on tawa/pan with little butter or ghee until golden on both sides.
OR use a sandwich toaster/grill.
Slice & serve hot!

Sprouted Matki Semi-Thick Gravy Recipe:
🕒 Prep Time: 10 mins
🍲 Cook Time: 20 mins
🍽️ Serves: 2–3
🌿 Ingredients:
Sprouted matki (moth beans) – 1 cup (well-sprouted)
Onion – 1 medium (finely chopped)
Tomato – 1 medium (chopped or pureed)
Ginger-garlic paste – 1 tsp
Green chili – 1 (optional, chopped)
Turmeric powder – 1/4 tsp
Red chili powder – 1/2 tsp (adjust to taste)
Coriander powder – 1 tsp
Cumin seeds – 1/2 tsp
Mustard seeds (optional) – 1/2 tsp
Asafoetida (hing) – a pinch
Salt – to taste
Oil or ghee – 1.5 tsp
Water – 1 to 1.5 cups (adjust for semi-thick consistency)
Fresh coriander leaves – for garnish
🍳 Instructions:
1. Cook the matki:
If not already cooked, pressure cook the sprouted matki with a pinch of salt and 1 cup water for 1–2 whistles (or simmer until soft but not mushy).
2. Temper the spices:
In a pan, heat oil.
Add cumin seeds (and mustard seeds if using). Let them splutter.
Add a pinch of hing.
Add chopped onion and sauté until light golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic & tomatoes:
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili. Sauté for a minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook until soft and oil starts to separate (or use tomato puree for smoother texture).
4. Add spices:
Add turmeric, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Mix well and cook for 1 more minute.
5. Combine matki & shimmer:
Add cooked matki (with water it was cooked in).
Add more water as needed for semi-thick gravy.
Let it simmer for 8–10 minutes on low heat. Mash a few beans lightly to thicken the curry.
6. Adjust salt and finish:
Check salt. Add more if needed.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
✅ Serving Suggestions:
Serve with phulka, roti, bhakri, or steamed rice.
Pair with a bowl of curd or salad for a balanced meal.

Lauki Drumstick Paneer Soup Bowl
🕒 Prep Time: 10 mins
🍲 Cook Time: 20 mins
🍽️ Serves: 2
🥦 Ingredients:
Lauki (bottle gourd) – 1 cup (peeled & chopped)
Drumsticks (moringa pods) – 1 long (cut into 3-inch pieces)
Paneer – 100 g (cubed or crumbled)
Ginger – 1/2 inch (grated)
Garlic – 3 cloves (chopped)
Black pepper powder – 1/2 tsp
Cumin seeds – 1/2 tsp
Olive oil / ghee – 1 tsp
Water or vegetable stock – 3 cups
Salt – to taste
Fresh coriander leaves – 1 tbsp (chopped)
Lemon juice – 1 tsp (optional, for freshness)
🍳 Instructions:
1. Prepare vegetables:
Peel and cube lauki.
Wash and cut the drumstick into 3-inch pieces.
Cube or crumble paneer.
2. Cook drumstick and lauki:
In a pressure cooker or pot, add lauki and drumstick pieces with 2 cups of water and a little salt.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles or simmer covered until soft (about 12–15 mins in a regular pot).
3. Extract drumstick pulp:
Once cooled, take the drumstick pieces, scrape or press out the soft pulp using a spoon.
Discard the outer fibrous shell.
Mash the lauki pieces lightly or blend for a smoother texture.
4. Sauté aromatics:
In a separate pan, heat oil/ghee.
Add cumin seeds, then sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant (1–2 mins).
5. Assemble the soup:
Add mashed lauki and drumstick pulp to the pan.
Pour in 1 more cup of water or stock for desired consistency.
Add paneer cubes or crumbles.
Simmer for 5–7 minutes.
6. Season and finish:
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Turn off the heat.
Stir in lemon juice and coriander leaves.
7. Serve:
Pour into soup bowls.
Garnish with extra paneer, coriander, or a dash of ghee if desired.

Lemon Coriander Veg Paneer Soup Recipe
🕒 Prep Time: 10 mins
🍲 Cook Time: 15 mins
🍽️ Serves: 2
🥗 Ingredients:
Paneer – 100 g (cut into small cubes or crumbled for a softer texture)
Carrot – 1 small (finely chopped)
Cabbage – 1/4 cup (shredded)
Capsicum (bell pepper) – 1/4 cup (chopped)
Spring onions or regular onion – 2 tbsp (chopped)
Garlic – 3 cloves (finely chopped)
Ginger – 1/2 inch (grated)
Fresh coriander leaves – 2–3 tbsp (finely chopped, with stems)
Lemon juice – 1–2 tsp (to taste)
Black pepper powder – 1/2 tsp (adjust to taste)
Salt – to taste
Olive oil or ghee – 1 tsp
Water or vegetable stock – 3 cups
👩‍🍳 Instructions:
Prep the veggies: Wash and finely chop all vegetables. Crumble or cube the paneer.
Sauté aromatics: Heat oil/ghee in a pan. Add chopped garlic, ginger, and onions. Sauté for 1–2 minutes.
Cook the vegetables: Add carrot, capsicum, and cabbage. Sauté for 2–3 minutes. Do not overcook — keep them slightly crunchy.
Add water or stock: Pour in 3 cups of water or stock. Bring to a boil.
Add paneer: Add crumbled or cubed paneer. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Season and simmer: Add salt, pepper, and coriander stems. Simmer for another 2 minutes.
Finish with lemon & coriander: Turn off the heat. Add fresh coriander leaves and lemon juice. Stir well.
Serve hot: Garnish with extra coriander and a lemon wedge if desired.

Healthy Ragi Veg Soup Recipe
🕒 Prep Time: 10 mins
🍲 Cook Time: 15 mins
🍽️ Serves: 2
🥦 Ingredients:
Ragi flour (finger millet flour) – 2 tbsp
Mixed vegetables – 1 cup (finely chopped: carrots, beans, capsicum, cabbage, spinach, etc.)
Water – 3 cups
Garlic – 2 cloves (minced)
Ginger – 1/2 inch (grated)
Green chili – 1 (optional, finely chopped)
Pepper powder – 1/2 tsp (adjust to taste)
Salt – to taste
Oil or ghee – 1 tsp
Lemon juice – 1 tsp (optional)
Coriander leaves – for garnish
🍳 Instructions:
Prepare the ragi slurry: In a small bowl, mix 2 tbsp ragi flour with 1/2 cup water. Stir well to avoid lumps. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Heat oil or ghee in a pot. Add garlic, ginger, and green chili. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add vegetables: Add the chopped mixed vegetables. Sauté for 2–3 minutes. Add a pinch of salt.
Add water & cook: Pour in 2.5 cups of water. Cover and cook for 5–7 minutes, or until the veggies are tender.
Add ragi slurry: Stir the ragi slurry again (it tends to settle). Slowly pour it into the soup while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Simmer: Let it simmer for 3–5 minutes, stirring often, until the soup thickens slightly.
Season: Add salt and pepper to taste. Turn off the heat. Add lemon juice if desired.
Garnish & serve: Garnish with chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot!

Corn and Spinach Soup Bowl
Mildly creamy, rich in fiber and antioxidants
📝 Ingredients (Serves 2):
1 cup spinach, chopped
1/2 cup  corn (boiled)
1 small onion, chopped
1 garlic clove
1 cup unsweetened almond milk or oat milk/ 1 tbsp corn starch
2 cups water or vegetable broth
Salt, pepper, and nutmeg to taste
🍳 Instructions:
Sauté onion and garlic in a pot for 2 minutes.
Add corn and spinach. Cook for 3–4 minutes.
Add milk/ corn starch and broth, season, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend smooth or leave chunky. Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Calories: ~150 per bowl ✅ Gut-friendly and light on the stomach

Protein-Packed Lentil Veggie Soup
Hearty, filling, and great for vegetarians
📝 Ingredients (Serves 2–3):
1/2 cup red lentils (masoor dal), rinsed
1/2 onion, chopped
1 tomato, chopped
1 carrot, diced
1 clove garlic, minced
3 cups water or veggie broth
1/2 tsp cumin seeds
Salt, pepper, turmeric to taste
Fresh cilantro
🍳 Instructions:
In a pot, sauté onion, garlic, cumin, and tomato for 3 mins.
Add carrots, lentils, turmeric, and broth.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 mins or until lentils are soft.
Blend partially for a thick texture. Garnish with herbs
Calories: ~180 per bowl ✅ High in plant protein and iron

3. Hearty Chicken & Veggie Power Bowl
Filling and balanced with a mix of fiber, protein, and slow-digesting carbs.
📝 Ingredients (Serves 3):
1 tsp olive oil
1/2 onion, chopped
1 garlic clove, minced
1 small carrot, sliced
1/2 cup chopped green beans
1/4 cup corn or peas
1 cup shredded chicken
1/2 cup cooked brown rice or lentils
3 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1/2 tsp paprika
Salt & black pepper to taste
Optional: A few spinach leaves or parsley to finish
🍳 Instructions:
Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion, garlic, and carrots for 4–5 minutes.
Add green beans, corn/peas, broth, and paprika. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add shredded chicken and cooked rice/lentils.
Simmer for another 5 minutes, season to taste, and serve hot.
Calories: ~250–280 per bowl
🥗 Great for meal prep — lasts 4 days in the fridge

Green Goddess Chicken Soup Recipe : (Blended Veggie + Chicken)
A creamy (but dairy-free!) soup packed with greens and nutrients.
📝 Ingredients (Serves 2):
1 tsp olive oil
½ onion, chopped
1 garlic clove
1 zucchini, chopped
1 cup broccoli florets
1 cup spinach
1 cup cooked shredded chicken
3 cups chicken broth
Salt, pepper to taste
Optional: 1 tbsp  2 tbsp oat milk for creaminess
🍳 Instructions:
In a pot, sauté onion and garlic in olive oil for 2–3 minutes.
Add zucchini, broccoli, spinach, and chicken broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer for 10–12 minutes.
Add cooked chicken, and blend about half the soup for a creamy texture (use an immersion blender or regular blender carefully).
Stir everything together, season, and serve.
Calories: ~180 per serving
🥄 Optional: Top with seeds or a spoon of Greek yogurt.

🌶️ 1. Spicy Slim-Down Chicken Soup Recipe:
A metabolism-boosting soup with bold flavors and a little kick.
📝 Ingredients (Serves 2–3):
1 tsp olive oil
½ onion, diced
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 carrot, diced
1 red bell pepper, sliced
1 small tomato, chopped (or ¼ cup canned)
½ tsp chili flakes (or to taste)
½ tsp cumin
1 cup shredded cooked chicken
3 cups low-sodium chicken broth
Salt and pepper to taste
Fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime (optional)
🍳 Instructions:
Heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, and carrot for 4–5 minutes.
Add bell pepper, tomato, chili flakes, and cumin. Cook for another 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth, add chicken, and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer for 10–12 minutes.
Serve with chopped cilantro and lime juice.
Calories: ~200 per serving
🔥 Tip: Add a little cayenne for more heat!

Zesty Lemon Chicken Veggie Bowl recipe:
A light, nourishing soup packed with veggies and a refreshing lemony twist — perfect for a healthy lunch or dinner when you're watching calories but want taste.
📝 Ingredients (Serves 2–3):
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 small onion, finely chopped
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 medium carrot, peeled and sliced
1 small zucchini, chopped
1 cup cooked, shredded chicken breast (grilled or poached)
3 cups low-sodium chicken broth
Juice of 1 lemon
Zest of ½ lemon
½ teaspoon dried oregano
Salt and black pepper to taste
Fresh parsley (optional, for garnish)
Optional: ¼ cup cooked quinoa or brown rice (for extra satiety)
🍳 Instructions:
Sauté the vegetables: In a medium-sized pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 2–3 minutes until translucent. Add the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
Add carrots and zucchini: Stir in the carrots and zucchini. Sauté for another 3–4 minutes until slightly softened.
Add chicken and broth: Pour in the chicken broth and bring the soup to a gentle boil. Lower the heat to a simmer and add the shredded chicken, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Simmer: Let it simmer for about 10–12 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the flavors have melded.
Add lemon: Stir in the lemon juice and zest. Taste and adjust seasoning — add more lemon juice if you like it zesty.
Serve: Ladle into bowls and top with fresh parsley.
🥣 Nutrition (Approx. per serving) :
Calories: 180
Protein: 22g
Carbs: 10g
Fat: 6g
Fiber: 2g

Cauliflower Peas Sabzi (Normal Healthy Version)
With onion and garlic – homestyle and flavorful
🧾 Ingredients:
Cauliflower – 2 cups, cut into florets
Green peas – ½ to ¾ cup
Onion – 1 medium, finely chopped
Garlic – 3 cloves, minced
Tomato – 2 medium, chopped or pureed
Green chili – 1, chopped
Ginger – 1 inch, grated
Cumin seeds – ½ tsp
Turmeric – ¼ tsp
Red chili powder – ½ tsp
Coriander powder – 1 tsp
Garam masala – ½ tsp
Salt – to taste
Oil – 1.5 tbsp
Fresh coriander – chopped
🍳 Instructions:
Clean cauliflower (same as above – hot salted water soak, optional but helpful).
Sauté aromatics:
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds.
Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent or golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and green chili. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes:
Add chopped or pureed tomatoes.
Cook until soft and oil begins to separate.
Add spices:
Turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Mix and cook 1-2 mins.
Add vegetables:
Add cauliflower and peas.
Stir well to coat with masala.
Cover and cook for 10–12 mins, stirring occasionally, until cauliflower is tender.
Finish:
Add garam masala and fresh coriander.
Serve with roti or rice

🌱 Cauliflower Peas Sabzi (Healthy Jain Style)
No onion, no garlic, sattvic-friendly
🧾 Ingredients:
Cauliflower (gobi) – 2 cups, cut into florets
Green peas – ½ to ¾ cup (fresh or frozen)
Tomatoes – 2 medium, finely chopped or pureed
Ginger – 1 inch, grated
Green chili – 1 (optional), chopped
Cumin seeds – ½ tsp
Asafoetida (hing) – a pinch
Turmeric powder – ¼ tsp
Red chili powder – ½ tsp
Coriander powder – 1 tsp
Garam masala – ½ tsp
Salt – to taste
Oil or ghee – 1 to 1.5 tbsp
Fresh coriander – chopped, for garnish
Lemon juice – optional
🍳 Instructions:
Prep cauliflower:
Rinse florets well and soak in hot salted water for 5 mins to clean. Drain and set aside.
Cook base:
Heat oil or ghee in a pan.
Add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add a pinch of hing, then ginger and green chili. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes:
Add chopped or pureed tomatoes.
Cook until they break down and become paste-like.
Spices:
Add turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Cook for 2 minutes.
Add vegetables:
Add cauliflower florets and peas. Mix well.
Cover and cook on low-medium heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cauliflower is tender.
Finish:
Sprinkle garam masala and chopped coriander.

Sprouted Matki Sabzi recipe  – Jain Style
🧾 Ingredients:
Sprouted matki (moth beans) – 1.5 cups (boiled or pressure-cooked)
Tomatoes – 2 medium, finely chopped or pureed
Ginger – 1 inch, grated

Salt – to taste

Boil the matki:
Pressure cook sprouted matki with a little salt and water (1–2 whistles) or boil in a covered pan until soft but not mushy. Drain excess water if needed.
Prepare the tadka (tempering):
Heat oil or ghee in a pan.
Add cumin seeds. Once they crackle, add a pinch of hing.
Add grated ginger and green chili. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Cook tomatoes:

Add turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes.

Mix well and simmer for 4–5 minutes to let flavors absorb.
Finish:

Garnish with fresh coriander and a dash of lemon juice (optional)

Makhana Porridge Recipe:
A creamy and nutritious breakfast option for those who want a slightly sweet dish.
Ingredients:
1 cup makhana
2 cups milk (or dairy-free milk like almond milk)
5–6 black raisins , pinch of saffron strands
1/4 teaspoon cardamom powder
A few chopped nuts (almonds, Pistachios) for garnish
Method:
Dry roast the makhana in a pan until it turns slightly golden.
Add milk to the pan and bring it to a boil.
Reduce the heat and let the makhana cook in the milk for 5-7 minutes until soft.
Add black raisins, saffron strands , cardamom powder, and mix well.
Cook for another 2-3 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Garnish with chopped nuts and serve hot.

Makhana Chivda Recipe:
A crunchy and spicy snack or breakfast dish that’s great during fasting.
Ingredients:
1 cup makhana (roasted)
1m  tbsp pumpkin seeds
1 teaspoon ghee
1/2 teaspoon mustard seeds
1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder
1/2 teaspoon red chili powder
Salt to taste
A pinch of black pepper
Fresh curry leaves (optional)
Method:
Heat ghee or oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, and let them splutter.
Add pumpkin seeds, curry leaves, and roast them for a minute.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, black pepper, and salt. Stir well.
Add the roasted makhana and toss everything together to coat the makhana with the spices.
Cook for 2-3 minutes on medium heat.
Serve as a crunchy snack or breakfast.

Makhana Ladoo Recipe:
Sweet, energy-boosting ladoos made with makhana, perfect for the fasting season.
Ingredients:
1 cup makhana (roasted)
1/4 cup grated coconut
1/4 cup jaggery (grated)
2 tablespoons ghee
1/4 teaspoon cardamom powder
A pinch of saffron strands (optional)
Method:
Roast the makhana in a pan until crispy. Grind it to a coarse powder in a blender.
Heat ghee in a pan, add grated jaggery, and melt it.
Add the makhana powder, grated coconut, and cardamom powder. Stir well until the mixture comes together.
Once it cools down slightly, shape the mixture into small ladoos.
Garnish with saffron strands if using and let them cool completely before serving.

Rajgira Paneer Paratha Recipe:
A filling and protein-rich paratha that's perfect for breakfast.
Ingredients:
1 cup rajgira flour (amaranth flour)
1/2 cup paneer (grated)
1 tablespoon ghee or oil (for cooking)
1/4 teaspoon cumin powder
1/4 teaspoon ajwain (carom seeds)
Salt to taste
Water (to knead the dough)
Fresh coriander leaves (optional)
Method:
In a mixing bowl, combine rajgira flour, grated paneer, cumin powder, ajwain, and salt.
Gradually add water and knead the mixture into a smooth, soft dough.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a small circle using a rolling pin.
Heat a tava or griddle, and cook each paratha with a little ghee or oil until golden brown on both sides.
Serve hot with a side of yogurt or chutney.

Sabudana and Paneer Salad Recipe:
A refreshing, protein-packed salad, perfect for light meals.
Ingredients:
½ cup sabudana (soaked)
60g paneer (cubed)
½ cucumber (chopped)
1 small tomato (chopped)
1 tablespoon lemon juice
Salt and pepper to taste
Fresh coriander leaves (optional)
Method:
In a bowl, combine the soaked sabudana, chopped cucumber, tomato, and paneer cubes.
Drizzle with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Toss gently and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

Rajgira Dosa (Amaranth Flour Dosa) recipe :
A healthy and gluten-free alternative to traditional dosas. Rajgira (also known as Amaranth) is packed with protein and nutrients, making it a great choice for fasting or just a nutritious meal.Ingredients:
1 cup Rajgira Flour (Amaranth Flour)
½ cup Samak Rice (Barnyard Millet) or Rice Flour (optional for crispiness)
1 tbsp Curd (optional, for fermentation)
1 small Potato, boiled and mashed (for softness)
1-2 Green Chilies, finely chopped (optional)
½ tsp Cumin Seeds
A pinch of Black Pepper (optional)
Salt to taste
Water as required
Ghee for cooking
Instructions:
Prepare the Batter:
In a mixing bowl, combine rajgira flour and rice flour (if using).
Add the boiled and mashed potato, curd, green chilies, cumin seeds, and black pepper.
Mix everything well, adding enough water to create a thin batter (similar to dosa batter consistency).
If using curd, let the batter rest for 20-30 minutes for light fermentation. If you're fasting, you can skip the curd.
Heat the Tawa:
Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) on medium heat and grease it lightly with oil or ghee.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the tawa and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin dosa.
Cook the Dosa:
Drizzle a little oil or ghee around the edges.
Cook on medium heat until the bottom side turns golden and crisp.
Flip and cook the other side for a minute or two, depending on the thickness.
Serve: Once crispy and golden, remove the dosa and serve hot.
Serve with: Coconut chutney/ green chutney /Peanut chutney/ Curd
This Rajgira Dosa is light, nutritious, and perfect for fasting (vrat) or as a gluten-free meal option. Enjoy!

Healthy Paneer Tikka Salad Bowl
📝 Ingredients

Healthy High-Protein Chicken Katsu Wrap

Season chicken with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Dip in egg white, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Air fry at 180°C (350°F) for 10–12 minutes, flipping halfway — or grill in a nonstick pan until crispy and cooked through.
Assemble the Wrap:
Warm the wrap slightly.
Spread mayo/Greek yogurt and drizzle katsu sauce.
Layer lettuce, cucumber, sliced chicken, and any optional toppings.
Wrap It Up:
Roll tightly like a burrito. Slice in half. Serve warm or chilled.

Granola Yogurt Jar Recipe

Add a layer of granola.
Add fruit.
Repeat with the remaining yogurt and a final sprinkle of granola on top.
Add Toppings:
Drizzle coffee and dark chocolate .
Sprinkle chia seeds, nuts, or cinnamon on top.
Serve or Store:
Eat immediately for crunchy texture.
Or seal and refrigerate for up to the next day (add granola last-minute to keep it crunchy).

Paneer Stir-Fry with Vegetables Recipe

Paneer Urban Salad Bowl Recipe

Chicken Whole Masoor Pulao Recipe.
🕒 Prep Time: 15 minutes
🕒 Cook Time: 30–40 minutes
🍽 Serves: 3–4
📝 Ingredients
For the Masoor + Chicken Base:
1 cup whole masoor dal (brown lentils) – soaked 3–4 hrs
300–400g bone-in or boneless chicken (skinless)(per serve 100g)
1.5 cups basmati rice or brown rice – soaked 20 mins (110g per serve)
2 medium onions – thinly sliced
2 medium tomatoes – chopped
1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
2–3 tbsp curd (yogurt) (optional, helps tenderize chicken)
2 green chilies – slit (adjust to taste)
Fresh coriander + mint leaves – handful each
1 tbsp ghee or oil (olive or mustard oil works too)
Whole Spices:
1 bay leaf
4–5 black peppercorns
2–3 cloves
1-inch cinnamon stick
1 black cardamom (optional)
1 tsp cumin seeds
Ground Spices:
1 tsp coriander powder
1/2 tsp turmeric
1/2 tsp red chili powder (adjust to taste)
1/2 tsp garam masala
Salt to taste
🔥 Instructions
1. Soak & Prep
Soak masoor dal for 3–4 hours and rice for at least 20 minutes.
Marinate chicken with curd, salt, turmeric, and ginger-garlic paste for 20 minutes (optional but helps tenderness).
2. Cook Chicken & Lentils
Heat ghee/oil in a large pressure cooker or heavy pot.
Add whole spices and sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add sliced onions and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, sauté for a minute.
Add tomatoes, green chilies, and ground spices. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Add chicken and stir for 5–7 mins until lightly browned.
Add soaked masoor dal + 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook:
Pressure cooker: 2 whistles on medium heat
Pot: Simmer covered for 15–20 mins until dal is almost tender
3. Add Rice & Simmer
Add soaked rice, salt, mint, coriander. Mix gently.
Add water: Use 1.5 to 2 cups water per 1 cup rice (adjust depending on rice type).
Bring to a boil, then lower heat.
Cover and cook until rice is done (12–15 mins).
4. Final Touch
Let it rest for 5–10 mins before fluffing.
Optional: sprinkle garam masala or lemon juice before serving.
🥣 Serving Suggestions
Serve with plain curd or raita (mint or cucumber)
Side salad: cucumber + carrot + lemon
Avoid fried accompaniments to keep it PCOD- and diabetes-friendly

Healthy Spinach Corn Chicken Sandwich

1 cup cooked and shredded chicken breast (skinless)
